chapter: 1977: Kansas City honor and the piano
title: The Kansas City tribute, birthday party and honorary doctorate
summary: Basie describes the tear-jerking October 30th celebration in Kansas City with old friends, Norman Granz, an honorary doctorate and the mayor's key.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: I just thought if you wanted to talk about what went on when you were out there and you were honored. This was October, right. Yeah, right, it was October 30th, I think.

Right. What do you mean, what went on? I think -- oh, I don't know, it was a beautiful thought and it was well planned and everything was a real great pleasant surprise and I really didn't think that -- I was really surprised to see how it grew.
I mean, just from the first thought that the guy had and -- but it all I think started from the foundation of Charlie and we did things out there a couple of years ago, and --
Yeah, and this gentleman had an idea

that he wanted to give me a birthday party, and I think it just turned around as he got to thinking about it, and he started to build on it, and made it a very beautiful thing, I mean, with all the stars that were there, that came through and went out and it was just a very big, thrilling thing.
It was a tear dripping thing, you know what I mean.

I had a few drops. It was real heavy and then getting the degree out at the university also, I mean, that was really -- but seeing all the guys, seeing like Sweets Edison (inaudible) and Lockjaw Davis and (inaudible) and Oscar Peterson, [Zoot] and then being close to the old guys in Kansas City, some who I worked with and some I have been around with for many years and (inaudible) Norman Granz who is the producer of [a man of] Pablo Capital Records who made it possible for Ella and Oscar and a couple of more people and maybe he saw to it that he didn't have them booked on the occasion, I mean, it would take at least four days away from their thing (inaudible) it was very nice of him to come along like that.
So now officially you're Dr. Basie?
Of course, you got any ailments.

No, they had planned on a motor thing, but nothing come of that, and it was just as well because I think it was a little wet -- but then it turned out to be marvelous and that little thing -- they had a little afternoon program and I met the Mayor and he gave me the key, was very nice man. He's an awful groovy man, that Mayor. He's very fine young and nice.
